title: CTCL / MF-SS Staging Algorithm (TNMB)
subtitle: ISCL/EORTC consensus staging — T, N, M, B classification to final stage

steps.prompt: What is the predominant skin lesion morphology?
steps.detail: Examine the full body surface. Distinguish patch (non-infiltrated, flat), plaque (indurated, elevated), and tumor (solid nodule >1 cm depth) lesions.

branches.label: At least one tumor ≥1 cm depth

steps.prompt: What percentage of body surface area (BSA) is involved by patches/plaques?
steps.detail: Use the rule-of-nines or palmar method (patient palm = ~1% BSA). Map and document all lesions. Assess at each visit for disease progression.

steps.prompt: T1 disease. Is there clinically abnormal lymphadenopathy?
steps.detail: T1: patch/plaque <10% BSA. Palpate all nodal basins. Lymph node >1.5 cm or palpably firm/fixed is abnormal.

steps.prompt: T2 disease. Is there clinically abnormal lymphadenopathy?
steps.detail: T2: patch/plaque ≥10% BSA. Lymph node assessment is mandatory. If nodes are suspicious on palpation or imaging, biopsy the most abnormal node.

steps.prompt: T3 disease confirmed. Is there visceral involvement on imaging?
steps.detail: T3: one or more skin tumors ≥1 cm. Obtain CT of chest, abdomen, and pelvis (or PET-CT). Visceral involvement = M1.

steps.prompt: T3 M0. Are there abnormal lymph nodes on exam or imaging?
Lymph node biopsy result (Dutch grade / NCI LN system)?
steps.detail: N1: dermatopathic changes, no lymphoma (Dutch grade 1). N2: early involvement, rare Reed-Sternberg-like cells (Dutch grade 2). N3: partial/complete effacement (Dutch grade 3-4). N4: frank lymphoma involvement (Dutch grade 4).

steps.prompt: N1/N2 lymph nodes. What is the T stage?
N3 disease. Check blood (Sézary count, flow cytometry, TCR clone)?
steps.detail: Peripheral blood staging: B0 = <5% atypical lymphocytes or <250 Sézary cells/mcL. B1 = 5-19% or 250-999 Sézary cells/mcL without significant clone. B2 = >1000 Sézary cells/mcL OR positive T-cell clone in blood with CD4:CD8 ratio >10, or CD4+CD7- >40%, CD4+CD26- >30%.

branches.label: B2 (high blood burden — Sézary syndrome criteria)

steps.prompt: T1 N0. Assess peripheral blood for atypical cells or Sézary clone.
steps.detail: In early-stage disease, blood involvement is uncommon but should be checked if there are suggestive clinical features (exfoliative erythroderma, pruritus). B0 = essentially no blood involvement.

steps.prompt: T2 patch/plaque. Assess peripheral blood for Sézary cells / clone.

branches.label: B0 N0 — no blood or node involvement

steps.detail: Stage IA: Patches or plaques on <10% BSA, no adenopathy, no visceral involvement, minimal or no blood involvement. Prognosis excellent; disease-specific survival near normal. Skin-directed therapy is standard first-line.
Stage IB: Patches or plaques on ≥10% BSA. Skin-directed therapy (NB-UVB, PUVA, topical steroids, mechlorethamine) with monitoring for progression. Median overall survival approximately 12 years.
Stage IIA: Patch/plaque (any BSA) with dermatopathic or early-involved lymph nodes. Combined skin-directed therapy; systemic agents (bexarotene, methotrexate) may be added for resistant disease.

Stage IIB: One or more skin tumors. Skin-directed therapy plus systemic agents. Brentuximab vedotin preferred if CD30 expression ≥10%. Mogamulizumab, bexarotene, IFN-alpha are options. Prognosis more guarded; median OS approximately 5 years.
Stage IVA1: Lymph node effacement (N3) without high blood burden. Aggressive systemic therapy warranted. Allogeneic HSCT may be considered in eligible patients with refractory disease.

steps.prompt: Stage IVA2 / Sézary Syndrome (T1-T4 N0-N3 M0 B2)
steps.detail: Stage IVA2: High blood burden (B2), fulfilling Sézary syndrome criteria when combined with erythroderma (T4). Extracorporeal photopheresis (ECP) is first-line for erythrodermic/Sézary disease. Mogamulizumab has demonstrated superior PFS vs vorinostat in this population. Allogeneic HSCT for fit patients.

steps.prompt: Stage IVB (any T, any N, M1, any B)
steps.detail: Stage IVB: Visceral (non-lymph node) involvement. Lung, liver, spleen most common. Systemic chemotherapy (gemcitabine, liposomal doxorubicin, CHOP-based regimens) or clinical trial preferred. Median survival <2 years; allogeneic SCT considered in eligible patients.
